title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: tree of life — continuation of sanctity not promised
pass_a_gloss: Relying on the same plural חַיִּים you will have it that the tree of life made for Adam a sure hope of continuing these lives. But it could not have made a sure hope of continuing the sanctity in which you place spiritual life. For God was demanding this continuation from Adam, not promising it to him: who if He had promised it would beyond doubt have made Adam impeccable: for the promise would have been ridiculous—I will bring it about that you persevere in sanctity and justice, provided you do not sin.
pass_b_english: On the same plural חַיִּים you would have the tree of life give Adam a sure hope of continuing these lives. It could not give a sure hope of continuing the sanctity in which you place spiritual life. God was requiring that continuance from Adam, not promising it to him. Had He promised it, He would beyond doubt have made Adam unable to sin—for the promise would have been absurd: I will make you persevere in sanctity and justice, provided you do not sin.
source_text: Eodem nixus plurali חַיִּים vis arborem vitae certam spem fecisse Adamo harum vitarum continuandarum. Atqui non potuit certam spem fecisse continuandae sanctitatis, in qua vitam spiritualem ponis. Hanc enim continuationem Deus ab Adamo exigebat, non ipsi promittebat: qui si eam promisisset, fecisset procul dubio Adamum impeccabilem: fuisset enim promissio ridicula, efficiam ut perseveres in sanctitate & justitia, modo ne pecces.

choices.choice: Continuation of sanctity demanded not promised; else impeccability

notes: Cap. IV Rursus observata densify section 217 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 190 tip–193 tip).
